passages.text: Before any site construction activity begins, the contractor must submit a task-specific safety management plan and obtain the superintendent's written approval of that plan. Mobilisation alone does not satisfy this condition.

The principal is not required to provide access to the work site until the contractor has delivered current certificates of currency for public liability, workers compensation, and contract works insurance.

The contractor must not discharge groundwater or treated construction water from the site unless the environmental representative has approved the discharge method and the required water-quality test results have been supplied.

Before excavation starts near an existing service, the contractor must locate the service, verify its depth, obtain the asset owner's isolation confirmation, and brief the excavation crew on the verified service route.

A traffic control plan accepted by the road authority must be in place before the contractor closes a traffic lane or changes a pedestrian route. The approved controls must be installed before the closure begins.
After practical completion, the contractor must provide an indexed completion report containing final test records, photographs, and signed inspection sheets.
The warranty period for installed equipment continues for twelve months after practical completion and restarts for an item that is replaced during that period.
A progress claim must identify work completed during the relevant month, approved variations, applicable retention, and the amount previously certified.
Design review comments do not transfer design responsibility to the principal. The contractor remains responsible for coordination and fitness for purpose.
When notified of a defect, the contractor must investigate its cause, propose corrective work, and complete the accepted correction within the directed period.
Materials stored on site must be protected from weather, separated from incompatible substances, and identified so that inspection records can be traced to each batch.
The monthly program update must show actual progress, forecast completion dates, the critical path, emerging delay risks, and recovery actions.
Formal notices must be addressed to the nominated representatives and delivered through the contract correspondence system with the subject and clause reference completed.
The environmental manager may audit erosion controls, waste records, noise monitoring, and incident close-out evidence at reasonable times.
Every worker attending the site must complete the project induction and sign the attendance record before entering an active work area.
The emergency response procedure identifies alarms, evacuation routes, assembly points, first aid contacts, spill response equipment, and incident notification duties.
